assertions.name: A6_correction_is_confined_to_the_pn_bond
assertions.source: pp/nn/spread/mirror all shift 0.0 exactly; magnitudes move up to 3.28% of AME

description: Settles the e_pn sign that qou-brng explicitly flagged open in commit 1b85370fd, by dissolving it. The framed bond ratio is EXACTLY linear in beta: z - beta h = (1-beta) z + beta (z-h), the two summands being the ratios of the pure crossings sigma (writhe +1) and sigma^-1 (writhe -1). The Markov trace is linear and the writhe factor (1-h)^(e/2) is defined per DIAGRAM, so the normalised bond is the sum of separately-normalised terms, not the whole ratio under an averaged exponent. The two forms agree exactly at beta = 0 and beta = 1 — which is why p-p and n-n cannot detect the difference and why an interpolation anchored on them reproduces itself. Forced back into exponent form, e_eff(beta_pn) = 0.149437, against +delta/2 = +0.000688 (interpolation, mine and brng's) and -delta/2 (production): 217x either, and both candidates are zero to three decimals. e_eff is concave (measured on a 99-point grid, all interior deviations positive, peak +0.14968 at beta = 0.54), so interpolation understates it everywhere between the endpoints. Worth 108x the sign dispute: dL_pn = 1.744e-2 (2.58%) against 1.613e-4 (0.024%), 0.292 MeV on 4He. The correction is exactly confined to the p-n bond: L_pp, L_nn, the L_nn - L_pp spread and the 3H-3He mirror difference all shift by 0.0, since p-p and n-n sit at the endpoints and p-n multiplicity Z.N is mirror-symmetric. This RETRACTS the +delta/2 half of framed_vs_writhe_normalised_bonds_probe.
caveats: THIS RETRACTS PART OF MY OWN PRIOR PROBE. framed_vs_writhe_normalised_bonds_probe derived e_pn = +delta/2 from the operator identity sigma - beta h = (1-beta) sigma + beta sigma^-1. The identity is correct and is reused here; what was wrong was feeding its coefficient average into an exponent. Read that probe's A2 as establishing that the bond is a MIXTURE, not as establishing a value for e_pn.

CONCAVITY IS MEASURED, NOT PROVED. e_eff(beta) - (1 - 2 beta) is positive at all 99 interior grid points and the endpoints are exact, which is enough to establish that interpolation understates e_eff at beta_pn — the only point the conclusion needs. The word 'concave' is a description of that grid, not a theorem.

SCOPE: this is a correction WITHIN the writhe-normalised convention only. Which convention binding should use is still the open physics question from framed_vs_writhe_normalised_bonds_probe (framing is Tw in Lk = Wr + Tw). The framed branch — bond constants, additivity, no-distance-decay — applies no normalisation and is untouched by everything here.

The isotope table is the NAIVE all-pairs sum in both columns, so it inherits the sub-additivity overstatement measured in pairwise_ceiling_is_overstated_probe and is not a binding prediction in either column. Only the DIFFERENCE between the columns is the quantity of interest.
